This was the second project after Wordle World. It focuses on preparing vocabulary for students taking the Chinese language test HSK. It covers all HSK levels from 1 to 6 and creates custom quizzes based on them. Quizzes include multiple choice, listening, and meaning. Users can track weak words and revise them instantly for better retention.
HSK Vocabulary is a language learning app for Chinese HSK exams. It has quizzes, progress tracking, and smart revision of weak words. It's in closed testing.
A vocabulary app for HSK levels 1–6, with custom quizzes (multiple choice, listening, meaning) and instant weak‑word revision.

Numatrix is another masterpiece that incorporates procedural content generation. Imagine a 10×10 grid where every number in every cell must be valid for its row and column arithmetic. This game generates a valid level within 1 second, and all arithmetic happens in real time. There's also an experimental mode 'Number Forge' that uses arithmetic operations to reach a specific goal.
It's a cross‑sum puzzle with algorithmic level generation. Each 10×10 grid is solvable and generated instantly. Number Forge adds a creative arithmetic mode.
Numatrix challenges players with grid‑based arithmetic where every cell matters. It uses PCG to create valid boards and includes a sandbox mode.

This is procedural generation on steroids… imagine a 5×5 grid where every cell contains a letter. It can either participate in making a word or not, but if it does, it must contribute to its row and column simultaneously. The main reason it's still under development is that a simple 5×5 grid level generation took 45 minutes. Ikhlaq is thinking of creating a model with pre‑trained data, but data creation is taking time due to limited resources and CPU power.

WordLock is a hardcore constraint‑satisfaction problem: generate a grid where every active letter forms valid words both across and down. Current algorithms are too slow (45 min for 5×5), so he's exploring ML‑assisted generation.
It's an in‑development puzzle generator. The challenge is simultaneous row/column word constraints. Ikhlaq is researching faster approaches, possibly using trained models.

This is a vocabulary building app, not ordinary flip‑card apps. It's a memory retention system with core neural anchor methods that permanently engrave words in the brain. It includes Observe, Listen, Read, Write, daily 5 words, and the Knowledge Tower where a wrong block collapses the tower. It also has quizzes, IELTS/TOEFL marking, certificates, and result sharing. It's currently in closed testing.

MemWord uses a four‑step Neural Anchor process to make words unforgettable. It includes speech recognition, daily practice, and a Knowledge Tower game to reinforce learning. It's highly effective and in closed testing.
This app is built for deep vocabulary retention using multi‑sensory methods and gamified revision. Features include Knowledge Tower, quizzes, and shareable results.

This is another ambitious project that will take a lot of time given the thought and effort required and overall complexity. The theme is simple: suppose you go back thousands of years in time and you have to explain the 21st century to the people of that time – not only explain but rebuild everything from scratch. This triggers users’ intrigue towards learning how things were actually built and how things work. This also has one of the greatest stories, and the story is in progress. This project incorporates all science and non‑science concepts.

Scientific Civilization is a large‑scale educational simulation where you rebuild technology from raw materials. It uses a technology‑dependency model and has a rich narrative. It's in pre‑production.
In this game, you time‑travel to an ancient village and must reconstruct modern science and technology. It combines resource management, experimentation, and a deep story.
